item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00418","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C19","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 is a clear substantive predecessor: it delegates presidential authority to the Secretary of Defense to order members and units of reserve components into active service without their consent, then permits delegation to the military-department Secretaries. The child reproduces this central legal machinery and much of its operative vocabulary while adapting the statutory source, eligible reserve category, duration, numerical ceiling, and presidential-approval limitation. C19 and C22 also concern delegating authority to order reservists to active duty, but they are confined to medical and allied specialists and lack C04's unit-based mobilization structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Secretary of Defense, and, when designated by him for this purpose, any of the Secretaries of the military departments ... are hereby authorized and empowered to exercise the authority vested in the President","parent_excerpt":"There is hereby delegated to the Secretary of Defense the authority vested in the President ... The Secretary of Defense is hereby authorized to redelegated ... to the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force","explanation":"Both establish a two-level delegation from the President to the Secretary of Defense and onward to the military-department Secretaries."},{"child_excerpt":"to order, without the consent of the persons concerned, any unit, and any member ... in the Ready Reserve ... to active duty for not more than 12 consecutive months","parent_excerpt":"to order into the active military or naval service ... for a period not to exceed twenty-four months, with or without their consent, any or all members and units of any or all Reserve components","explanation":"This is the same distinctive operative mechanism: involuntary activation of reserve members and units for a specified maximum term."},{"child_excerpt":"However, the Secretary of Defense may not order any unit ... to active duty ... under this section without the approval of the President.","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of Defense is hereby authorized to redelegated, subject to such conditions as the Secretary may deem appropriate","explanation":"Both separately regulate the treatment of delegated unit-activation authority, although the child substitutes presidential approval for the parent's discretionary redelegation conditions."}]}
